title: US Civil Rights Movement
key_facts: Mass movement to end racial segregation and discrimination against African Americans.
Key moments included Brown v. Board of Education (1954), the Montgomery Bus Boycott (1955–1956), and the March on Washington (1963).
Major federal laws included the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965.
Used nonviolent protest, legal challenges, and grassroots organizing to challenge Jim Crow laws.
causes: Long history of slavery, segregation, and racial violence in the United States.
Exclusion of African Americans from political power, quality education, and economic opportunity.
Contradiction between American democratic ideals and racial inequality, especially after World War II.
Growing activism from Black churches, civil rights organizations, and youth movements.
outcome: Legal end to de jure segregation in public facilities and schools.
Expansion of Black voting rights and political representation, especially in the South.
Creation of federal enforcement mechanisms against discrimination.
Inspired later social movements for gender equality, LGBTQ+ rights, and disability rights.

figures.name: Martin Luther King Jr.
figures.role: Civil rights leader and Baptist minister
figures.significance: Advocated nonviolent resistance; led the Montgomery Bus Boycott and March on Washington.

figures.name: Rosa Parks
figures.significance: Refused to give up her bus seat in Montgomery, helping spark the bus boycott.

figures.name: Thurgood Marshall
figures.role: NAACP attorney and later Supreme Court Justice
figures.significance: Argued Brown v. Board of Education, which declared segregated schools unconstitutional.

figures.name: John Lewis
figures.significance: Key organizer in the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee (SNCC) and Selma marches.

impacts: Transformed US law by prohibiting segregation and discrimination based on race in many areas of public life.
Shifted national attitudes on race and justice, though inequality persisted.
Created enduring civil rights organizations and a model for nonviolent protest worldwide.
Brought racial injustice to global attention during the Cold War.
